system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: **L1 — Index** | Lives in the system prompt | The model on every turn | 3 lines / ~60 tokens per skill
system_prompt_style.note: README only. It says a per-installed-skill L1 index block is inserted into the system prompt. The prompt-building source (src/context.ts, src/agent.ts) was not in the evidence.

env_context_strategy.note: Inferred from file names only: tools glob/grep/ls/read. The README says the model sees 'just one Bash'. The default tool list and task template were not available.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: Long sessions auto-compress history; tokens never overflow, memory never lost
context_compaction.note: The README marks live history compaction as beta. The mechanism (summary vs truncation) is not visible; summarize is the closest reading of the prose.

observation_format.evidence_quote: The model sees the error and asks you to grant — never silently fails.
observation_format.note: Bash stdout and skill results are described as text. The observation conversion code was not available.

tool_call_format.note: A tools-list entry named Bash suggests a provider tool call. Skill verbs are issued as shell command lines. The parser source was not available.

tool_count.note: The README says the model sees one Bash tool, but src/tools contains bash, edit, glob, grep, ls, read, skillCall and write, and src/subagent contains agentTool. The default tool array was not in the evidence.

edit_primitive.note: src/tools/edit.ts and src/tools/write.ts exist but their contents were not available.

tool_schema_source.note: The schema-producing code was not available.

protocol_standardization.note: The README mentions MCP only as a contrasting skill type. No source or dependency file was available to grep.

loop_primitives.note: Inferred from file names only: loops simple, chain, evaluator, orchestrator, parallel, route. The default is presumably simple (react). The loop code was not available.

planning_granularity.note: No plan object or prompt text was available.

multi_agent_topology.note: src/subagent/* and src/loops/orchestrator.ts exist, but the default agent configuration was not available.

delegation_mechanism.note: Inferred from file names only (agentTool, runAgent, builtinAgents). Whether this is on by default is unknown.

human_in_loop.note: A permission prompt UI exists. The README also describes install-time capability grants by the user.

short_term_state.note: The state object source was not available.

long_term_memory.note: Installed skills persist under ~/.yome/skills and are indexed into the system prompt. Thread history is also stored per cwd.

state_persistence.note: threads/ session history and SessionPicker.tsx exist, but the resume code path was not visible.

self_verification.note: src/loops/evaluator.ts exists but its contents were not available.

rollback.note: 'yome skill rollback' reverts skill installs, not run changes.

execution_isolation.note: Commands run on the host shell. Skills run AppleScript on the user's machine.

filesystem_access.note: The README states fs:read/fs:write are scope-limited for skills only. Raw Bash filesystem scope is not stated.

network_policy.note: A 'network' capability exists for skills. The Bash egress policy is not stated.

permission_model.evidence_quote: Every skill must declare the OS resources it needs in its manifest, and the user must grant them explicitly at install time.
permission_model.note: The capability grants act as a static allowlist. src/permissions/ruleParser.ts suggests rule-based permissions, possibly a policy_engine. src/yomeSkills/blacklist.ts also exists.

tracing.note: Sessions are stored in ~/.yome/threads, but their format was not visible.

guardrails.note: src/redact.ts redacts shared case bundles; this is not a model-output filter.

target_domain.evidence_quote: Drives native apps via AppleScript / Win32 / DBus
target_domain.note: The domain is desktop productivity via native apps (ppt, mail, calendar), which is not an exact fit for any listed value.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: export YOME_PROVIDER=anthropic # or openai (auto-detected from base URL)
model_agnostic.note: Two provider protocols are supported, with an arbitrary base URL.
